content.thinking:
All the key findings are confirmed in s05. Now let me note important details for the usbvision finding in s05:

- Line 1437-1438: the model-driven branch `interface = &dev->actconfig->interface[usbvision_device_data[model].interface]->altsetting[0];` — this is the if-alt-count branch (interface array indexing), not mine.
- Line 1458: `if (interface->desc.bNumEndpoints < 2)` — validates the *initially selected* interface's altsetting[0].
- Lines 1497-1515: `uif = dev->actconfig->interface[0]` (interface[0] always exists per USB config parser — at least one interface guaranteed? Actually in s01 finding f002 said "interface[0] always exists (config parser guarantees at least one interface)"). The loop over `usbvision->num_alt = uif->num_altsetting` reads `uif->altsetting[i].endpoint[1].desc.wMaxPacketSize` — fixed index 1 with NO bNumEndpoints check per iteration. The check at line 1458 was on a possibly DIFFERENT interface (`interface` may be the model-driven one or ifnum one; uif is hardcoded interface[0]).

Note in s05 usbvision is in drivers/media/usb/usbvision (not staging). Good — in scope for media-epidx.

Now, one caveat: is `interface` (line 1437ff) the same as `uif` (interface[0])? The bNumEndpoints < 2 check at 1458 applies to `interface`, which is `&dev->actconfig->interface[<model or ifnum>]->altsetting[0]`. For most models, `.interface == -1` and ifnum is the probed interface number. The probed interface for usbvision devices is typically 0. So when ifnum==0 and interface[0] has >= 2 endpoints in altsetting[0], the later loop over interface[0]'s altsettings [i] for ALL i still lacks per-altsetting checks. A malicious device with altsetting[0] having 2 endpoints but altsetting[3] having 0 endpoints → OOB read at line 1509. This is exactly the s01 finding (f002/i005's sibling f005 finding 1 was this same site in s01 at lines 1497-1515).

Let me also double-check the uvc site (line 1281 guarded by bNumEndpoints==1 check at 1280 — safe) and usbtv (guarded). And check remaining media-usb drivers I haven't: em28xx (loops bounded), stk1160 (loops bounded), tm6000, zr364xx, pwc, s2255, au0828, hdpvr, siano (loops bounded; smsusb.c:423 udev->ep_in[1] — noted in f002 as device-maintained array NULL deref — actually let me look at smsusb.c:423: `le16_to_cpu(dev->udev->ep_in[1]->desc.wMaxPacketSize)` — udev->ep_in is the device-wide endpoint pointer array indexed by endpoint NUMBER (address & 0xf), not the descriptor flex array. ep_in[1] can be NULL if device has no IN endpoint number 1 → NULL deref at plug-in. That was noted in f002/i002 as "not a descriptor-array flex-index read" — outside my branch invariant strictly (it's an assumed endpoint number into udev->ep_in[], whose entries are set from descriptors). Hmm. The branch description says "probe/bind/init or stream-start code that indexes altsetting[i].endpoint[k].desc.bEndpointAddress or .wMaxPacketSize with a literal or driver-assumed k ... without first checking altsetting[i].desc.bNumEndpoints > k". The udev->ep_in[1] access is indexing the device's endpoint array by endpoint number without checking existence — closely related (missing guarantee: endpoint 1 IN exists). f002 explicitly left it "to other branches since it is not a descriptor-array flex-index read". I'll examine it and classify as a candidate — it's in the media tree and is a plug-in-triggered NULL-deref of descriptor-derived data. I could report it as an additional finding or mark safe/unresolved. Let me read it.

Also tm6000-cards.c:1165 `curr_e->desc.wMaxPacketSize` — need to check how curr_e is obtained. Let me look. And check cpia2, go7007, ttusb-budget, ttusb-dec, as102, hackrf, airspy, msi2500, pulse8-cec, pvrusb2, stkwebcam for endpoint indexing.
